newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ING remains overweight on Brazil stock market.
newsitem.headline: ING remains overweight on Brazil stock market.

text.p: ING Barings said it remains positive on Brazil's stock market, despite the 12 percent drop taken by the Ibovespa index in the past two days, maintaining its overweight position in Brazil.
Paulo Vasconcellos, head of Brazil Equity Research, said the current market decline is based on profit-taking due in part to mostly unfounded fears that the Brazilian real currency may be devalued.
ING Barings said it views the recent market weakness as a good buying opportunity.

Brazilian stocks fell by 8.51 percent on Tuesday, with the Bovespa index posting its biggest single-day drop since January 1995, amid concerns that the moves by speculators that forced some Asian countries to devalue their currencies in recent weeks could also spread to Brazil.
In three sessions, stocks fell over 14 percent.

Mauro Schneider, senior economist at ING Barings in Brazil, said in a statement the probability of a successful speculative attack on the real is quite low, although the currency's present overvaluation makes it vulnerable to devaluation.

In addition, the Brazilian government has more leeway than Thailand and the Philippines, which have become the target of speculative attacks, to raise interest rates and defend the real currency, he noted.

Schneider said Brazil's fundamentals have not changed recently, with the current account deficit at $15.6 billion in the first half or 4.19 percent of gross domestic product and positive preliminary trade figures for July.

Considering Brazil's current market declines, ING Barings also said it had upgraded Brazilian telecommunications firm Telebras, which is the most traded share in the Sao Paulo bolsa, to buy from hold based on the stock's weak performance since last week.
Telebras preferred closed off 8.23 percent at 145 reais Tuesday.
